title: The portability check flags the {/< escapes its own message recommends, because it scans decoded text nodes
description:
FOUND IN THE FIELD by opum-doc (lore 0.12.0, measured 2026-10-01 02:50Z on its branch docs/ODOC-364-ripgrep-research), relayed by opum-agent; INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED here 2026-10-01 on a fixture of my own, dev source and released 0.12.0 identical.

THE DEFECT. mdxHazardFindings (src/core/check.ts, ~line 1436) warns when a mdast **text** node's value contains a raw `<` or `{`. mdast decodes character references into text-node values, so a source `{` arrives decoded as `{` and is flagged; likewise `<`. The finding's own message says "escape it ({) or wrap the text in backticks" -- and the FIRST of those two remedies does not clear the warning. Only backticks do.

FIXTURE (temp bundle, one file per shape; source binary and released 0.12.0 identical):
  probe/raw-brace.md       "A raw { brace in prose."                    -> warns (correct control)
  probe/backtick-brace.md  "A backticked `{` brace."                    -> no warning (correct control)
  probe/escaped-brace.md   "An escaped { brace in prose."          -> WARNS (wrong: the recommended escape)
  probe/escaped-angle.md   "An escaped < angle in prose."            -> WARNS (wrong)
  probe/escaped-plain.md   "The tools are {grep, ag, ...}"    -> WARNS (wrong; the field shape)
  probe/escaped-in-link.md "[{grep, ag, git grep}](https://example.com/)" -> WARNS (wrong; the field shape)

WHY IT MATTERS. In MDX it is the source-level `{` that starts a JSX expression, and character references are decoded after parsing, so `{` in source is portable -- the warned documents are fine to ship, and the check contradicts the portable subset its own message names. `lore check --strict` fails on them, so an author who follows the message escapes and stays red, or restructures correct prose. One of the two is wrong and it is the flag, not the message.

CLASSIFICATION: a reproducible defect -- the tool contradicts its own documented behaviour, the remedy it prints.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fixture whose only `<`/`{` occurrences are character references -- in prose and inside link text -- produces no portability finding, while raw `<`/`{` in prose still warns; both controls live in the same case, so a mutation that stops flagging raw characters is red too.
Both remedies the finding message names actually clear the warning: escaping (`{`/`<`) and backticks, asserted for each of the two characters.
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.

plan: 1. Fix mdxHazardFindings to scan each text node RAW SOURCE span, not mdast decoded value; thread the body source through portabilityScan.

2. Add AC#1 (references in prose + link text produce no portability finding; raw chars still warn -- both controls in one case) and AC#2 (escaping and backticks clear the warning, for both characters).
3. Mutation-test: revert to node.value, confirm exactly those two tests red.
4. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Fixed entry; the portable-markdown spec already states escaping is portable, so it needs no change.
5. Gates: full bun test suite + bun run lore check (AC#3), lint, typecheck. Review, record, land.
implementationNotes: Completed on branch fix/LCLI-663-mdx-hazard-source-not-decoded. ROOT CAUSE: mdxHazardFindings scanned each mdast text node value, and mdast DECODES character references before a value reaches the scanner, so a source `{`/`<` arrived as a literal `{`/`<` and was flagged -- the check flagged the very escape its own message names. FIX: the scan now reads each text node SOURCE span (threaded from the parsed body via a new rawSourceOf helper), so references pass and source-level `<`/`{` still warn. EVIDENCE: test/check.test.ts AC#1 (references in prose AND link text produce no portability finding; raw chars still warn -- both controls in one case) and AC#2 (escaping and backticks clear the warning for both characters). MUTATION: reverting the scan to node.value reds exactly those two tests (314 pass / 2 fail); with the fix 316 pass / 0 fail. DOCS: no change needed -- docs/reference/portable-markdown.md:145 already states escaping IS portable, so the SPEC was right and the CHECK was wrong; the fix aligns the check with it. CHANGELOG: [Unreleased] Fixed entry added. GATES (AC#3): full suite 4982 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; bun run lore check exit 0; lint and typecheck clean.
finalSummary: lore check portability warnings now judge the MDX raw-< and raw-{ hazard from the SOURCE span of each mdast text node rather than its decoded value, so character references ({, <) are no longer flagged while raw < and { in prose still warn. Why: the check contradicted both its own printed message and docs/reference/portable-markdown.md, which name escaping as a valid remedy -- an author who followed the printed remedy stayed red, or restructured correct prose. Verified by two new tests (references in prose and link text produce no finding, with raw-character controls in the SAME case so the test is not silent; escaping and backticks clear the warning for both characters), mutation-tested red exactly; full suite 4982 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail and lore check exit 0. Run job-0ac7fxs.
